question: Should experiment-gated Claw lifecycle diagnostics be accepted as a core Doctor contribution that can make `openclaw doctor` report warnings and return nonzero for enabled experimental users?
rationale: The patch is an additive experimental product surface rather than a repair to an established contract; source-level correctness evidence does not decide whether core Doctor should own this lifecycle policy.

options.title: Accept the core Doctor boundary
options.body: Approve the experiment-gated contribution, subject to resolving the stacked predecessor and retaining its advisory, read-only behavior.

options.title: Keep diagnostics outside core Doctor
options.body: Ask for the lifecycle status to remain in the Claw CLI or another extension surface rather than adding an ordered core Doctor contribution.

recommendation.title: Accept the core Doctor boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the experiment-gated contribution, subject to resolving the stacked predecessor and retaining its advisory, read-only behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review directly established the runtime correctness requirements for the diagnostic’s Gateway and state-observation boundary.
